data.title: Vasa’s VS-041 shows positive Phase Ic results in HFpEF trial
data.description:
Vasa Therapeutics has reported positive topline findings demonstrating clinical proof of concept for its lead therapy, VS-041, in a Phase Ic study in patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF).

The randomised, placebo-controlled trial (NCT07219511) evaluated the narrow-spectrum matrix metalloproteinase (MMP) inhibitor at two dose levels in patients receiving background guideline-directed medical therapy for the heart condition.

VS-041 proved safe and well tolerated while lowering NT-proBNP, an established biomarker of cardiac wall stress and heart failure, among the treated patients.

The study showed the utility of serum endotrophin via the NordicProC6 assay to detect patients with fibroinflammation. Analyses of extracellular matrix collagen turnover and exploratory clinical measures will follow in early 2027.

Vasa Therapeutics CEO and co-founder Artur Plonowski said: “Vasa had three important goals for the recently completed Phase Ic trial in patients with HFpEF.

“First, we showed that narrow-spectrum MMP inhibition is safe and well tolerated in a population of HFpEF patients with increased risk of unfavourable outcomes, and the reduction in NT-proBNP, achieved within 28 days, suggests a compelling path forward in the clinic.

“Secondly, we demonstrated that serum endotrophin can be used prospectively to identify an endotype of HFpEF patients that cannot be characterised by clinical data alone. This novel enrichment strategy should translate to smaller and potentially faster development.”

The oral compound gained fast track designation (FTD) from the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) in November 2025, following a Phase I trial in healthy volunteers (ISRCTN15814719).

That early study confirmed safety at doses matching preclinical efficacy, where the molecule ameliorated cardiac fibrosis and improved diastolic relaxation in models of the progressive heart disorder.

Co-funded by the European Regional Development Fund and the Polish National Centre for Research and Development, VS-041 also targets fibroinflammation in chronic kidney disease and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

Privately held Vasa Therapeutics focuses on cardiovascular and muscle ageing, advancing a pipeline of four assets addressing heart failure, life-threatening arrhythmias, peripheral arterial disease, rare neuromuscular diseases, and sarcopenia.

data.title: Lilly reports promising 52-week results from TOGETHER-PsA trial in PsA
data.description:
Eli Lilly and Company has reported promising 52-week results from the Phase IIIb TOGETHER-PsA trial assessing Taltz (ixekizumab) alongside Zepbound (tirzepatide) for active psoriatic arthritis (PsA) in adults with overweight or obesity.

The multicentre, randomised, open-label, assessor-blinded study (NCT06588296) evaluated subcutaneous Taltz in combination with Zepbound, compared with Taltz alone, in participants advised to reduce their calorie intake and exercise.

The trial enrolled 271 adult patients with active disease and a body mass index (BMI) of at least 30kg/m², or 27 to under 30kg/m² alongside a weight-related comorbidity.

The primary endpoint assessed the proportion of patients who achieved both a 50% improvement according to American College of Rheumatology criteria (ACR50) and at least a 10% reduction in body weight at week 36.

Exploratory 52-week results revealed 39.2% of patients receiving the combination therapy achieved this dual metric, compared to 1.7% of individuals who received the monotherapy.

Furthermore, 43.7% of patients receiving dual therapy achieved an ACR50 response at one year, compared with 15.7% of those receiving Taltz alone.

Weight reductions of 10% or greater occurred in 85.7% of combination participants and 6.7% of monotherapy patients by week 52.

Lilly Immunology’s development senior vice president Mark Genovese said: “It’s remarkable to see the durability of efficacy and breadth of outcomes with Taltz and Zepbound at one year in measures that matter most to patients with psoriatic arthritis and obesity or overweight, from improvements in disease control to physical function and fatigue,

“Data from TOGETHER-PsA continue to evolve our understanding of immunometabolic health and show what may be possible for patients when these chronic conditions are treated together to address the combined disease burden.”

Exploratory analyses showed minimal disease activity (MDA) was attained by 28.2% of dual-treatment patients versus 13.6% for monotherapy at week 52.

Reported adverse events (AEs) were mostly mild to moderate, reflecting the recognised safety profile of each compound without presenting unexpected safety signals.

Frequent AEs affecting at least 5% of combination patients included constipation, diarrhoea, dizziness, headache, injection site reactions, nausea, sinusitis, urinary tract infections, and vomiting.

For patients receiving monotherapy, reported adverse events occurring in at least 5% comprised arthralgia, diarrhoea, injection site reactions, and upper respiratory tract infections.

Baseline patient BMI averaged 37.6, matching broader clinical contexts where around 65% of PsA cases in the US feature concurrent obesity or overweight.

In September this year, Lilly reported findings from an indirect treatment comparison analysing data from the ACHIEVE-3 and PIONEER PLUS studies of its investigational therapy Foundayo (orforglipron) against oral semaglutide in adults with type 2 diabetes.

data.title: Zhimeng Biopharma concludes enrolment in ALS trial of CB03-154
data.description:
Shanghai Zhimeng Biopharma has completed patient enrolment in the pivotal Phase II/III clinical trial of its investigational potassium-channel opener, CB03-154, for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS).

A total of 255 patients have been recruited across 15 clinical research centres in mainland China, and Professor Fan Dongsheng of the 3rd Affiliated Hospital of Peking University is the principal investigator.

The trial’s primary efficacy endpoint is the change from baseline in Revised Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis Functional Rating Scale (ALSFRS-R) score at week 39.

Discovered and developed by Zhimeng Biopharma independently, CB03-154 showed neuroprotective effects on motor neurons through modulation of neuronal excitability, restoring the balance between excitation and inhibition, in preclinical studies.

Zhimeng Biopharma founder and CEO Dr Huanming Chen said: “I would like to extend my sincere appreciation to Professor Fan Dongsheng and the investigators at all clinical research centres across China for their dedicated efforts, as well as to all ALS patients and their families who participated in the trial for their selfless commitment.

“Moving forward, we will spare no effort to advance clinical development and regulatory submissions, striving to bring a truly effective new treatment option to ALS patients in China and around the world as soon as possible.”

The China Centre for Drug Evaluation (CDE) approved the initiation of the Phase II/III ALS trial in July 2025. The US Food and Drug Administration had previously granted CB03-154 orphan drug designation in October 2023.

If Phase II top-line data prove positive in the third quarter of 2027, the company intends to file a marketing application with the China CDE seeking conditional approval.

Zhimeng Biopharma said this approach is designed to give ALS patients earlier access to innovative treatments, reflecting its patient-centred development philosophy in rare diseases.

Beyond ALS, CB03-154 is advancing through clinical development in additional central nervous system (CNS) indications. As of October 2026, the drug had entered Phase II trials for focal epilepsy in both Australia and China.

data.title: Teva to halt Phase II MSA therapy trial after futility analysis
data.description:
Teva Pharmaceuticals has announced plans to halt a Phase II clinical trial evaluating emrusolmin (TEV-‘286) to treat adults with multiple system atrophy (MSA), after an interim analysis found the study was unlikely to meet its primary efficacy endpoint.

The decision followed a recommendation from the independent data monitoring committee (IDMC), which conducted a prespecified interim futility analysis of the TOPAS-MSA study.

IDMC’s review met the predefined futility criterion, suggesting a low probability of demonstrating efficacy if the trial continued.

Teva noted this was a predictive assessment rather than a final efficacy analysis. No safety concerns arose from the interim review.

An investigational, orally administered small molecule, emrusolmin targets alpha-synuclein aggregation, a core pathogenic mechanism expected to be involved in MSA, a rare neurodegenerative disorder. Teva is developing the therapy in collaboration with privately managed biotechnology company MODAG.

The randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled TOPAS-MSA trial is designed to enrol nearly 350 participants.

They were to receive either 300mg of emrusolmin or placebo for roughly 48 weeks, followed by a follow-up period of four weeks.

The primary endpoint measured change from baseline to week 48 in the modified Unified Multiple System Atrophy Rating Scale Part I score.

Teva global R&D executive vice-president and chief medical officer Eric Hughes said: “While we are disappointed by the outcome of this interim analysis for the Phase II study, we remain deeply committed to learning everything we can from these data.

“We are deeply grateful to the patients, families, investigators, and study teams who contributed their time and commitment to this research. Our hope is that the science and learnings can deepen our understanding of MSA and help us determine a path forward for emrusolmin.”

Teva said it would work with study investigators to ensure protocols are followed as the trial ends. The company also plans to share the findings with the scientific community after concluding a comprehensive analysis.

It said that the discontinuation applies only to the TOPAS-MSA study and does not represent a final decision on the emrusolmin programme as a whole.

Last month, Sanofi and Teva’s inflammatory bowel disease drug showed benefit in patients with both ulcerative colitis and Crohn’s disease.

data.title: Mondego Bio begins Phase Ia trial of oral MB‑388
data.description:
Mondego Bio has initiated a first-in-human Phase Ia clinical trial of MB‑388, an oral dual protein tyrosine phosphatase non-receptor type (PTPN2/PTPN1) inhibitor, which is designed to act in both tumour cells and immune cells to overcome resistance to cancer immunotherapy.

The placebo-controlled, randomised, double-blind trial is assessing MB‑388’s single and multiple ascending doses in healthy volunteers.

It aims to evaluate the therapy’s tolerability and safety, characterise its pharmacokinetics, and measure target engagement using blood-based pharmacodynamic biomarkers.

The company anticipates initial human pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic results in December 2026.

Mondego Bio subsequently plans to start a Phase Ib trial in January 2027 for patients with advanced solid tumours who progressed during or after standard treatment, including checkpoint inhibitors.

After monotherapy dose levels are cleared, the trial will incorporate a combination run-in with programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-(L)1) blockade covering both checkpoint-naive and checkpoint-refractory patients.

Readout from combination dose escalation is scheduled for December 2027.

Mondego Bio CEO Nikolay Savchuk said: “Starting the first clinical study of MB‑388 is an important milestone for Mondego. The Phase Ia study will define the relationship between exposure, pathway engagement and tolerability, giving us the data to move efficiently into our planned study in patients with cancer.”

In preclinical tumour models that responded or resisted PD-1 blockade, MB‑388 showed activity as a single agent and in combination with anti-PD-1 therapy, increasing intratumoral cluster of differentiation 8 (CD8)-positive T cells and granzyme B.

When tested against osunprotafib, a clinical-stage PTPN2/PTPN1 inhibitor, MB‑388 demonstrated higher oral exposure, longer target coverage, and a substantially higher unbound fraction in human plasma.

Based in Portugal, Mondego Bio focuses on developing small-molecule therapies that restore interferon-gamma signalling, increase antigen presentation, and enhance natural killer and T-cell function.

The company was founded with support from Biovance Capital, OrbiMed, and Torrey Pines Investment, with co-investment from the Fundo de Capital e Quase Capital, which is managed by Banco Português de Fomento and supported by the InvestEU Fund.

data.title: Tango and Erasca’s Phase I/II trial of ERAS-0015 combo opens for enrolment
data.description:
Tango Therapeutics and Erasca have begun enrolment for a Phase I/II trial assessing the combination of oral therapies ERAS-0015 and vopimetostat in patients with lung and pancreatic cancers.

The multi-centre, open-label trial focuses on individuals diagnosed with methylthioadenosine phosphorylase (MTAP)-deleted pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, alongside patients with MTAP-deleted and rat sarcoma virus (RAS)-mutant non-small cell lung cancer.

It is sponsored by Tango Therapeutics and consists of dose-escalation and expansion phases.

The dose-escalation phase primarily aims to identify the combination’s maximum tolerated dose.

Secondary measures include evaluating safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, and antitumour activity.

Tango Therapeutics president and CEO Malte Peters said: “The encouraging clinical activity, durability and tolerability observed to date with vopimetostat in combination with RAS inhibition reinforce our belief that co-targeting PRMT5 and RAS represents a promising new frontier in the treatment of pancreatic cancer and potentially other RAS-driven cancers.

“We are thrilled to initiate this study in partnership with Erasca, a company leading the advancement of RAS-targeted therapies, to evaluate vopimetostat with ERAS-0015 and further explore the potential of this clinically validated and synergistic combination approach.”

Both investigational therapies target cancer pathways through distinct mechanisms.

ERAS-0015 is an oral pan-RAS molecular glue created to block RAS signalling and counter resistance to mutant-selective inhibitors by suppressing RAS wild-type variants.

Erasca is currently assessing the therapy in the AURORAS-1 Phase I trial for patients presenting with RAS-mutant solid tumours.

Initial dose escalation demonstrated linear pharmacokinetics alongside confirmed and unconfirmed partial responses at doses starting at 8mg once daily.

Vopimetostat is a once-daily oral protein arginine methyltransferase 5 (PRMT5) inhibitor evaluated by Tango Therapeutics as both a monotherapy and in combination.

In clinical evaluations to date, the therapy showed durable activity and a favourable tolerability profile across several MTAP-deleted cancers, including pancreatic and lung malignancies.

data.title: Merck begins Phase III ENHANCE-3 trial of Ohtuvayre in COPD
data.description:
Merck & Co (MSD) has begun the Phase III ENHANCE-3 clinical trial assessing Ohtuvayre (ensifentrine) to prevent exacerbations in adults with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD).

Patient recruitment has begun, with the initial participants enrolling in the US.

The placebo-controlled, randomised, double-blind study plans to enrol around 2,136 patients across 28 countries.

Eligible participants are adults aged 40 to 80 years with a verified COPD diagnosis for at least 12 months, a current or previous smoking history, and a documented moderate or severe exacerbation within the prior year while receiving standard care.

Individuals must have received consistent background therapy for at least two months. Subjects will be randomised 1:1 to twice-daily Ohtuvayre or placebo alongside their existing standard-of-care regimen.

The primary endpoint assesses the annualised rate of adjudicated moderate or severe exacerbations over 52 weeks.

Secondary measures examine overall safety and adjudicated severe exacerbations over 52 weeks, and quality of life through the St George’s Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ) at week 24.

Permitted standard treatments include inhaled corticosteroids, long-acting beta-agonists, and long-acting muscarinic antagonists, or bronchodilators alone if corticosteroids are inappropriate.

MSD Research Laboratories global clinical development vice-president Dr Mahesh Patel said: “Many patients with COPD continue to experience persistent symptoms such as shortness of breath, despite current standard-of-care therapy. For these patients, exacerbations remain a major driver of disease progression and diminished quality of life.

“The initiation of the Phase III ENHANCE-3 study marks an important step in our efforts to further strengthen the body of evidence supporting Ohtuvayre and its potential to address significant unmet needs in COPD care. We remain committed to advancing innovative research to help the millions of people impacted by this disease worldwide.”

The US Food and Drug Administration approved Ohtuvayre in June 2024 for adult COPD maintenance based on data from the ENHANCE-1 and ENHANCE-2 studies.

Last month, MSD reported that the Phase IIb MK-7240-012 study of its investigational humanised monoclonal antibody, tulisokibart, achieved its primary endpoint for patients with moderate to severe hidradenitis suppurativa.

data.title: Lipocine doses first patient in Phase III postpartum depression study
data.description:
Lipocine has dosed the first patient in a Phase III trial assessing LPCN 1154 (oral brexanolone) for the treatment of postpartum depression (PPD).

The outpatient, placebo-controlled Brexanolone Lifting Outcomes of Moms (BLOOM) trial (NCT07822321) will assess the therapy as a 48-hour oral course designed for at-home administration.

It is expected to enrol around 120 patients, with topline findings anticipated in the second half of 2027.

BLOOM will examine the primary efficacy endpoint through change from baseline in the 17-item Hamilton Depression Rating Scale (HAM-D17) total score at 60 hours after treatment begins.

Lipocine aims to use the resulting safety and efficacy data to complement an existing clinical package to the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for a potential new drug application (NDA) under the 505(b)(2) pathway.

Lipocine president and CEO Dr Mahesh Patel said: “Our goal is to develop a treatment that provides rapid symptom relief through a 48-hour oral course taken at home.

“We believe the BLOOM Phase III study is designed to promote study enrolments that are representative of the actual patient population of postpartum depression and provide confidence in data quality.”

The new trial integrates adjustments following an earlier Phase III study, which did not meet its primary endpoint in the full analysis set, though post hoc findings and safety results supported continued development.

Feedback from a meeting with the FDA confirmed the necessity of a positive, well-controlled Phase III trial, while indicating that the remainder of the 505(b)(2) application package appeared complete.

To mitigate placebo response, BLOOM incorporates centralised rating for screening, fewer rating scales, decreased patient interaction with site staff, and standardised participant education.

Operational controls also include third-party site selection, participation by academic centres, geographic diversity, participant limits per site, and prespecified sensitivity analyses covering outlier sites and pharmacokinetic data.

LPCN 1154 is an unapproved oral formulation of brexanolone that is a chemical match to allopregnanolone, a neuroactive steroid modulating gamma-aminobutyric acid type A (GABA-A) receptor.

PPD is a serious condition that can cause persistent sadness, anxiety, daily impairment, and thoughts of self-harm.

data.title: Vir Biotechnology’s hepatitis D drug scores in Phase II and Phase III trials
data.description:
Vir Biotechnology’s investigational combination of elebsiran and tobevibart for chronic hepatitis delta (CHD) has met its primary endpoint in a Phase III trial, while a Phase II trial saw 100% of patients treated with the combination achieve undetectable viral levels.

The topline findings of Phase III ECLIPSE 1 (NCT06903338) were presented during an oral session at the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD) The Liver Meeting 2026 in Denver, Colorado.

The pivotal study demonstrated that 44% of patients receiving monthly subcutaneous injections of elebsiran and tobevibart attained undetectable virus alongside alanine aminotransferase (ALT) normalisation at week 48.

In comparison, no participants in the delayed treatment group achieved this outcome at week 12.

The trial also achieved its key secondary endpoint, with 79% of treated participants reaching undetectable viral levels at week 48 against 0% in the comparator arm.

Among patients receiving the combo, hepatitis delta virus ribonucleic acid (HDV RNA) target not detected (TND) was noted in 85% of the 46 patients with cirrhosis and 73% of the 37 patients without.

In terms of safety, the investigational combination was well-tolerated.

The trial recorded one Grade 3 treatment-related adverse event (TRAE) involving a transient decrease in neutrophil count that resolved within 15 days, with no therapy interruptions or treatment discontinuations occurring.

Transient flu-like symptoms after the initial dose represented the most frequent adverse reaction.

Vir Biotechnology president and CEO Marianne De Backer said: “Our ambition in hepatitis D has always been to fundamentally change what patients can expect from treatment.

“These compelling ECLIPSE 1 results deliver on the potential for elebsiran’s and tobevibart’s complementary mechanisms to drive the virus to undetectable levels, potentially lowering the risk of progression to cirrhosis, liver cancer and liver-related mortality.

“We believe the robust viral suppression combined with the flexibility of monthly at-home or healthcare provider administration has the potential to position elebsiran and tobevibart as the best-in-disease treatment for hepatitis D.”

Vir Biotechnology also reported expanded results from the Phase II SOLSTICE trial (NCT05461170) of elebsiran and tobevibart for CHD, where all 28 patients completing 96 weeks of treatment achieved undetectable viral levels.

In an exploratory cohort of ten individuals who discontinued treatment after maintaining viral suppression for 96 weeks, all 10 achieved sustained viral response at 12 weeks without rebound.

Under a December 2025 licensing deal, Norgine holds commercial rights for the therapies in Australia, Europe, and New Zealand.

data.title: OncoC4 announces positive Phase I/II findings for cesalatamig in NSCLC
data.description:
OncoC4 has reported positive findings from Phase I/II trials of its investigational bispecific antibody, cesalatamig (AI-081), as a monotherapy in patients with pre-treated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).

The study evaluated patients with programmed cell death ligand 1 (PD-(L)1)-resistant/refractory NSCLC.

In an efficacy-evaluable group of 55 patients, the antibody showed dose-dependent antitumour activity across three evaluated cohorts administered every three weeks.

Objective response rates (ORR) assessed by investigators were 10% in the 1mg/kg cohort of 10 patients, 21% in the 3mg/kg cohort of 24 patients, and 33% in the 10mg/kg cohort of 21 patients. Disease control rates (DCR) were 40%, 67%, and 90%, respectively.

Responses occurred across different PD-L1 expression levels, and exposure-response analyses supported selecting the 10mg/kg dose for subsequent clinical testing.

OncoC4 co-founder, CEO and chief scientific officer Yang Liu said: “These findings strengthen the rationale for advancing cesalatamig monotherapy in previously treated NSCLC.

“The clinical results and exposure-response analyses support the selection of 10mg/kg every three weeks as the dose for our planned pivotal study and provide a clear path forward for the continued development of cesalatamig in this setting.”

These pooled findings were derived from the open-label, multicentre, global BiPAVE-001 (NCT06635785) and BiPAVE-001 CN (CTR20253261) Phase I/II studies, with data recorded up to 31 July 2026.

The safety dataset comprised 103 NSCLC patients who received at least one monotherapy dose at 1mg, 3mg, 10mg, or 20mg/kg every three weeks.

Cesalatamig monotherapy was well tolerated across all tested dose tiers, and safety profiles were comparable between squamous and non-squamous disease.

Of these participants, 77 (75%) had non-squamous tumours, 25 (24%) had squamous tumours, and one patient had an unknown histology.

A baseline ECOG performance status of 1 was documented in 77% of patients. Participants had received a median of two previous lines of systemic therapy, and 42% had received three or more lines.

Cesalatamig is a tetravalent bispecific antibody targeting PD-1 and vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF).

OncoC4 is evaluating the antibody in China and the US across Phase I dose-escalation and Phase II dose-optimisation stages in advanced solid tumours, as monotherapy and in combination with standard care.

In September 2026, the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) granted cesalatamig fast track designation for NSCLC that has progressed following platinum-based chemotherapy and PD-(L)1 immunotherapy.
